comparisonV1:
Create ONE landscape, two-panel educational illustration for The Vegetable Guru gardening book. It is a paired comparison of DIGGING (left) and NO-DIG (right). No lettering, labels, numbers, borders, arrows or watermark anywhere. Transparent background. The two panels must be separate with ample empty space between, same scale, same viewpoint, same size and equally healthy small leafy green plants in each. Each panel should fill about 40% of canvas width with 8% safe outer margins; keep all silhouettes complete.
Reference images 1 and 2 are approved HOUSE DRAWING STYLE ONLY, not subject: bold simplified dimensional vector-like illustration, generous broad colour and shadow planes, lively saturated greens, cream tapered highlights. Translate this to warm brown soil, dark brown compost and simple green seedlings. Clean shapes and restrained modelling; no black outlines, no fine stippling, no busy roots, no glow, no photographic texture.
Subject: two small rectangular soil bed cutaway blocks, each drawn at a low three-quarter angle with a visible front cross-section and top surface. Neither bed has a timber frame. Native soil is warm brown throughout, dark compost a distinct deeper brown. No rocks, gravel or invented drainage layer.
LEFT: an established bed with compost mixed into the topsoil, indicated by several broad dark-brown patches distributed through the upper brown soil, with three small healthy generic leafy plants growing in the surface. Add a modest recognisable garden spade leaning BESIDE the block, its full shaft and handle visible, never piercing a plant. Lower soil brown.
RIGHT: identical size bed and matching three small healthy plants, with an intact continuous dark-brown compost dressing on TOP of the undisturbed warm-brown soil. Show simple roots passing from the compost into the brown soil, a few broad clean root lines only. NO cardboard in this established bed diagram, NO fork, NO spade. It should not appear taller or healthier than the left; the comparison is method, not yield.
Instructional precision and simple readable layer contrast matter. Attractive bold garden illustration matching the actual references. Landscape composition around 2:1, no titles.

noDigSequenceV1:
Create ONE educational gardening illustration containing exactly THREE evenly spaced panels in a single horizontal row, landscape ratio about 3:1. Transparent background, no text, no letters, no numbers, no arrows, no borders. This is a step sequence for starting a no-dig vegetable bed on lawn, to be printed across a 160 mm wide book page. Panel centres at one sixth, one half and five sixths of canvas width. Each panel confined to its own third, with clear transparent gap. Same little rectangular open-sided bed throughout, no timber edging, same viewpoint and scale. All complete silhouettes inside generous safe margins.
Use supplied approved carrot and beetroot illustrations for HOUSE STYLE ONLY: bold simplified dimensional graphic shapes, broad flat colour planes and controlled shading, rich warm brown earth, dark brown compost, bright green leaves, clean cream highlights. No photographic textures, no painterly noise, no black outlines, no excessive fine detail. Drawing to be attractive and legible when small.
LEFT PANEL: three or four flat tan cardboard sheets with visibly overlapping edges laid directly over closely cut green grass, forming a rectangular bed footprint. A small rolled/curling corner may show the underlying grass; most surface covered. No compost yet. There is no tape, plastic or staples. Cardboard lies flat on lawn, not buried under soil.
MIDDLE PANEL: the same footprint now covered with a generous, level DARK BROWN mature compost layer, with a very thin tan cardboard edge visible underneath at its front. Under that, existing native brown soil with grass only OUTSIDE the bed. One plain wooden-handled garden rake shown resting at the edge, tool complete. Compost is the growing surface, no additional soil above it, no gravel beneath it. Slightly sloping open sides.
RIGHT PANEL: the same bed, same dark surface compost layer above thin cardboard and existing soil, now planted with three small fresh green vegetable transplants. Show a recognisable small hand trowel beside it, not poking through the cardboard. New transplants with several leaves each, no adult crop. No roots drawn through cardboard because this depicts immediate planting. No extraneous tools, sacks or people.
These are a clear three-stage overview, not three competing options. The layer order must be accurate: new compost on top; thin cardboard directly beneath compost; existing ground below. NO drainage stones or artificial extra layers. Keep all panels the same visual size. No quantities embedded.
diggingSequenceV1:
Create ONE educational gardening illustration containing exactly THREE equally sized panels in a single horizontal row, wide landscape about 3:1, transparent background. No text, labels, letters, numbers, arrows, borders or watermark. This is a simple SINGLE-DIGGING vegetable bed sequence. Each stage in its own third of canvas, with clear gaps. Same rectangular open-sided ground bed, warm brown topsoil over slightly darker native subsoil, no timber frame, identical scale and three-quarter viewpoint. All tools and soil kept wholly in frame.
Use the supplied approved carrot and beetroot as HOUSE STYLE only. Bold clean dimensional vector-like forms with broad colour planes, controlled shadows and cream highlights. Simple recognisable warm wooden handles, forest green and muted steel tool parts. Simplify earth into broad clods, no tiny gravel, no painty texture or fine noise, no black outlines. Do not copy vegetables from references; small generic young leafy plants only where specified.
LEFT: a cleared rectangular soil bed, with a shallow rectangular trench dug across the NEAR end, the depth of ONE spade blade only. The brown topsoil removed from this trench is neatly piled on the ground just BESIDE the bed. The empty trench has a visible flat base in undisturbed darker soil. A complete garden spade stands beside the stored pile. A small amount of dark compost is scattered thinly on remaining upper bed surface. No deep second trench; no plants in this panel.
MIDDLE: same bed, digging has progressed to its middle. One open trench goes across the bed. On its near side, the earlier trench is filled with turned, loose warm brown TOPSOIL containing dark compost flecks. On its far side, the topsoil is still unturned. A recognisable full garden spade holds ONE brown clod just over the open trench, poised to drop it from the next row into the open space. Keep trench only one spade blade deep. Undisturbed darker subsoil remains under the entire bed; do not mix it upward. The stored small soil pile is still beside bed. No plants, no cardboard.
RIGHT: same bed now complete, all trenches filled with warm brown topsoil, flat finely raked top, no open holes and no separate soil pile left. A complete modest wooden-handled rake lies beside the finished bed. Three small generic green vegetable transplants just planted at even spacing in the bed. No cardboard, no continuous black mulch band: organic matter is MIXED into brown topsoil as modest dark patches. This indicates the bed is ready to plant after settling.
The reader must recognise saving first trench soil, turning successive rows into the preceding trench, and finishing/planting. No double digging and no buried drainage layer. Match the three-panel no-dig page in visual weight.
